title: Lead Quantity Surveyor
description: Job Highlight This is a unique opportunity for a seasoned Lead Quantity Surveyor to significantly contribute to sustainable development initiatives across the Horn of Africa. The role offers the chance to apply expert knowledge in cost management and quantity surveying to high-impact infrastructure projects, work within a dynamic international environment, and advance a career with a leading UN organization dedicated to improving lives. Role Purpose The Lead Quantity Surveyor manages the comprehensive quantity surveying and cost management processes for civil engineering projects, providing authoritative advice and adapting established methodologies to ensure accurate cost estimation, procurement support, and financial control. This role is critical for the successful and efficient delivery of infrastructure initiatives, ensuring integrity, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness. Functions / Key Results Expected Site Assessment and Data Review Undertake complex/multi-site technical assessments and establish approaches/methodologies. Provide senior technical advice on the interpretation of drawings, surveys, specifications, geotechnical information, and other technical data to inform project design and cost decisions. Establish appropriate methodologies and approaches for quantity assessment, measurement, and cost estimation for complex infrastructure projects. Identify and proactively address technical, constructability, and cost risks, recommending mitigation measures and alternative solutions. Actively participate in multidisciplinary technical coordination and resolve complex technical issues. Engineering Estimates and Cost Planning and Analysis Lead and validate complex, high-value estimates and provide authoritative cost advice.. Provide authoritative technical advice to project management and senior stakeholders on quantities, cost estimates, technical specifications, pricing assumptions, and Bills of Quantities. Develop cost breakdowns using current market prices, labor rates, and material costs. Review and challenge estimates prepared by project teams or consultants, ensuring technical integrity, consistency, competitiveness, and value for money. Bills of Quantities (BoQ) Preparation Establish and promote standardized measurement methodologies, item descriptions, units, and quantity take-off approaches across projects. Ensure consistency and technical integrity between drawings, specifications, design changes, BoQs, and cost estimates. Provide technical leadership in resolving complex discrepancies between design documentation, specifications, quantities, and cost estimates. Develop guidance and quality-control mechanisms to improve the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of BoQs and quantity assessments. Procurement Support Provide authoritative technical advice to tender documents, including BoQs and specifications throughout procurement and bid evaluation . Advise on responses to bidder queries during the procurement process. Advise project and procurement stakeholders on cost competitiveness, technical compliance, risks, and value-for-money considerations. Review proposed contractual rates and commercial assumptions and advise on their technical and financial implications. Site Measurement and As-Built Quantification Advise on cost variation analysis, contractors’ claims analysis and new rate review during implementation, including advice on possible resolution Review and validate proposed new rates and cost adjustments, ensuring consistency with contractual provisions, market conditions, and established pricing methodologies. Provide senior technical recommendations on disputed quantities, variations, claims, and cost adjustments to support management decision-making. Lead the preparation and validation of as-built quantity assessments and ensure alignment with approved designs, site measurements, and contractor submissions. Provide technical advice supporting the certification and acceptance of completed work Documentation and Reporting Establish and oversee technical quality-control mechanisms for engineering estimates, BoQs, quantity measurements, cost data, and related documentation. Develop and maintain technical standards, procedures, guidance, templates, and tools for quantity surveying and engineering cost management. Establish and maintain reliable cost databases, benchmarks, historical pricing information, and lessons learned to support future infrastructure projects. Prepare high-level cost analysis and management reports, highlighting trends, risks, variances, and implications for project delivery. Provide senior management with advice and recommendations on project cost, commercial risks, and technical matters. Promote knowledge sharing and provide technical guidance and mentoring to project teams and less experienced personnel in engineering estimating, quantity surveying, measurement, and cost control. Education Requirements Required An Advanced University Degree (Master’s degree

data warehouse architecture and ETL/ELT processes feeding BI, analytics, and reporting layers Support integration efforts by ensuring proper data availability and quality Implement event-driven architectures (Kafka, Pulsar, CDC) Maintain semantic layers, metadata catalogs, data dictionaries, and embedding pipelines Guarantee data consistency, quality, and structuring across all storage environments System Reliability, Monitoring & Observability Monitor system health, performance, uptime, and data flow Implement observability for databases, pipelines, and agentic workflows Conduct audits, performance reviews, and capacity planning Troubleshoot incidents, perform root-cause analysis, and implement corrective actions Security, Access Control & Compliance Manage roles, permissions, RBAC/ABAC, and secure system access Ensure compliance with data security, privacy, and auditability requirements Maintain explainability and traceability of agentic and automated actions Apply best practices for backups, encryption, and data lifecycle protection Automation, Infrastructure & DevOps Support Develop scripts for automation (Bash, Python, PowerShell) Support IaC approaches using Terraform and Ansible Assist in container deployment workflows (Docker, Kubernetes) Provide configuration-level support for ExtJS or Django-based platforms Collaboration & Documentation Work closely with engineering, data, and business teams Maintain documentation of schemas, workflows, contracts, and governance Provide knowledge support and system enablement to internal teams Requirements WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR 5+ years of experience in System administration Strong proficiency in SQL and relational database optimization Experience with vector databases and embedding search systems Experience with NoSQL databases (MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch) Knowledge of OLAP databases

title: Lead Structural Engineer
description: Job Highlight This is an exceptional opportunity for a seasoned Structural Engineer to lead the design and technical oversight of impactful infrastructure projects in the Horn of Africa. The role offers the chance to apply advanced engineering expertise to complex challenges, contribute to the region's development, and collaborate with diverse teams within a leading international organization, fostering professional growth and making a tangible difference in communities Role Purpose The Lead Structural Engineer manages and provides authoritative advice on structural design projects, adapting existing policies and approaches to meet emerging client and project needs within the Horn of Africa. The incumbent is responsible for independently performing structural analysis, developing design solutions, ensuring compliance with international standards, and supervising technical aspects of project delivery, thereby contributing to the successful implementation of UNOPS' infrastructure mandate. Functions / Key Results Expected Site Assessment and Site Investigation Follow-up Review site conditions including topography, terrain, and existing infrastructure to identify design constraints. Interpret topographic surveys, geotechnical reports, and relevant environmental data to support design decisions. Assess site-specific risks such as settlement, slope instability, and groundwater conditions. Evaluate soil properties and bearing capacity to inform foundation design. Support feasibility assessments and selection of appropriate structural systems. Structural Design Perform structural system selection, structural design and analysis of buildings and civil works, including superstructure and foundation systems under relevant load combinations. Develop structural solutions that are safe, durable, efficient, and constructible. Ensure appropriate consideration of load paths, stability, serviceability, and material performance. Apply relevant international and national design standards and codes. Design Deliverables Prepare structural drawings, design calculations, design reports, presentations, design brief, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities (BoQs). Ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance of all design outputs. Address design review comments and update deliverables accordingly. Maintain organized and traceable documentation of all design work. Procurement Support Provide technical input to tender document preparation, including specifications and BoQs. Support clarification of technical queries during the bidding process. Assist in the technical evaluation of proposals where required. Construction Support and Quality Assurance Respond to design clarification requests; Revise designs; Provide details when requested by the Project Implementation team Review shop drawings, method statements, and material submissions. Support resolution of technical issues encountered on site. Review as-built drawings and contribute to progress and quality reporting. Provide technical support during construction to ensure compliance with design intent and specifications. Coordination and Technical Interface Work closely with multidisciplinary teams including architectural, geotechnical, and MEP disciplines. Ensure proper integration of structural systems within the overall project design. Participate in technical discussions and coordination meetings as required. Knowledge Management Maintain proper documentation of structural design outputs and reports. Contribute to knowledge sharing and continuous improvement within the team. Education Requirements Required An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline, with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience, is required. A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline, combined with a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Required Experience Requirements Relevant professional experience in the structural design of buildings and civil works is required, including experience in the design and analysis of reinforced concrete and/or steel structures; preparation of structural drawings, design reports and Bills of Quantities (BoQs); use of structural design software such as ETABS, SAP2000, SAFE, Robot, or equivalent; and interpretation of topographic surveys and geotechnical investigation reports. A valid practicing professional Structural Engineering license is required (please attach to application). Desired Experience in infrastructure or public facility projects, international design standards, and/or working with the United Nations is desirable.

title: Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) Specialist
description: The Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) Specialist is responsible for implementing, monitoring, and continuously improving health, safety, and environmental programs for MAXAM's explosives and blasting operations at the Allied Gold mine site (Kurmuk). The position ensures compliance with company standards, client requirements, and applicable legal and regulatory obligations related to the transportation, storage, handling, and use of explosives. The incumbent serves as the primary HSE focal point between MAXAM and Allied Gold, promoting a strong safety culture, managing operational risks, supporting environmental compliance, and ensuring the safe and efficient execution of blasting activities. Key Responsibilities Implement and monitor MAXAM's Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) management systems at the Allied Gold project site. Ensure compliance with company policies, client (Allied Gold) requirements, and applicable legal and regulatory standards governing explosives and blasting operations. Conduct HSE inspections, audits, hazard identification, and risk assessments for explosives storage, transportation, charging, and blasting activities. Monitor and promote safe work practices, including adherence to permit-to-work systems, PPE requirements, and critical safety controls. Investigate incidents, near misses, environmental events, and blasting-related occurrences, and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions. Coordinate and deliver HSE inductions, training programs, toolbox talks, and safety awareness initiatives for employees and contractors. Monitor environmental aspects of blasting operations, including vibration, air overpressure, dust, noise, and fly rock, and ensure compliance with environmental requirements. Support emergency preparedness and response activities related to explosives, blasting operations, transport incidents, fires, and other site emergencies. Serve as the primary HSE liaison between MAXAM and Allied Gold, participating in client meetings, inspections, audits, and performance reviews. Prepare and maintain HSE reports, records, statistics, and compliance documentation, ensuring accurate and timely reporting. Promote continuous improvement and a proactive safety culture to achieve operational excellence and zero-harm objectives. Minimum Qualification Requirements Education Bachelor's Degree in one of the following: Occupational Health and Safety Environmental Health, Environmental Science, Mining Engineering, Geological Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering Related discipline Experience Required Minimum 5 years of HSE experience in mining, explosives, construction, heavy industry or related sectors. Minimum 3 years of direct experience in explosives, blasting or mining contractor operations. Experience working under a contractor-client operating model. Experience interfacing with mine owner HSE teams. Experience in ISOs9001, 14001, 45001. Not required but is a plus if you have this certificates: -NEBOSH International General Certificate (IGC) -NEBOSH Diploma (often preferred for H&S Manager roles) -ISO 45001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer -IOSH Managing Safely (more often for supervisors than managers) -Mine rescue, emergency response, or first-aid qualifications relevant to the operation Preferred Open-pit mining experience. Experience with MMU operations and bulk explosive systems. Experience supporting large-scale gold mining operations.

title: Group Supply Chain & Logistics Manager
description: Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Employment Type: Full-Time Reports to: Group Chief Operating Officer Required No.: 1 About The Role & Our Client On behalf of our client, a diversified Ethiopian business group operating across agriculture, coffee processing and roasting, trading, export, and related commercial activities , we are seeking an experienced Group Supply Chain & Logistics Manager to lead and optimize the Group's end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations. The role will have a strong focus on international export and import operations , while overseeing logistics, warehousing, inventory, fleet, trade documentation, and supply chain planning across multiple business units. The successful candidate will work closely with Finance, Sales & Marketing, Procurement, Operations, Quality, and external stakeholders to ensure efficient, compliant, and cost-effective movement of products and materials. Key Responsibilities Supply Chain & Logistics Management Develop and implement integrated supply chain and logistics plans aligned with business requirements. Optimize transportation, warehousing, inventory, distribution, and logistics costs. Establish effective SOPs, controls, and performance standards across supply chain operations. Identify operational risks, bottlenecks, and opportunities for continuous improvement. Export & Import Operations Manage end-to-end export and import operations from order confirmation through final delivery. Coordinate international shipments, container positioning, freight forwarding, customs clearance, and transportation. Ensure accurate and timely preparation of export and import documentation. Monitor vessel schedules, shipment status, delays, and delivery requirements. Coordinate with shipping lines, freight forwarders, clearing agents, banks, regulators, and international customers. Ensure compliance with Ethiopian and international trade requirements. Trade Finance & Compliance Coordinate trade finance requirements with Finance, including LC, CAD, TT, and related documentation. Ensure export documentation meets contractual and banking requirements. Monitor regulatory requirements and minimize risks related to documentation errors, delays, penalties, and demurrage. Warehouse, Inventory & Fleet Oversee inventory control, warehouse operations, stock reconciliation, and export readiness. Manage transportation and fleet utilization, maintenance, fuel efficiency, and operating costs. Strengthen systems for inventory accuracy, traceability, asset utilization, and accountability. Leadership & Performance Lead and develop the Group Supply Chain & Logistics team. Establish KPIs and monitor supply chain, logistics, transportation, and inventory performance. Prepare management reports and provide strategic recommendations to the Group COO. Drive cost optimization, process improvement, and operational efficiency. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, International Trade, Business Administration, Finance, Procurement, or a related field. title: Head of Finance, Multilevel Partnerships
description: PLEASE NOTE: Submit applications to INGA Talent and Advisory; details below in the “How to Apply” section. This is a hybrid position which requires 8 days per month in the office. You can be based in our office in London, the Hague, Addis Ababa, or Nairobi. About The Program Since launching in 2023, the Coalition for High Ambition Multilevel Partnerships (CHAMP) for Climate Action has quickly developed into the primary platform for multilevel climate partnerships. With 77 endorsing countries and the EU, CHAMP aims to unlock the potential of multilevel partnerships to accelerate NDC implementation, improve access to climate finance for subnational governments, and showcase pioneering action on climate mitigation and adaptation. World Resources Institute (WRI) serves as a key partner supporting CHAMP's governance, diplomatic engagement, communications, and national action. Job Highlight As the Head of Finance, Multilevel Partnerships, you will serve as the organisational lead for CHAMP's subnational climate finance agenda, providing strategic oversight and technical leadership to global and country efforts to close the subnational climate finance gap through policy influence, advocacy, and implementation support. Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance and Private Sector, and working closely with the Senior Urban and Regional Economist and the NDC Partnership, this position requires expertise in public and blended finance, strong diplomatic skills to engage with Ministries of Finance, multilateral banks, and development finance institutions, and the ability to turn country-level lessons into systems-level change. What You Will Do Programme Delivery (60%) Lead design, delivery, and monitoring of Climate Finance workstream to ensure coherence between global finance reform efforts, country platform design, and on-the-ground technical assistance in Kenya and Colombia. Produce actionable analysis and insights capturing enabling conditions for subnational climate finance, drawing from country experiences and global practice, and translate findings into practical recommendations for governments and finance actors. Organise annual knowledge exchange series for national and subnational officials, country platform coordinators, development banks, and funders to share lessons on subnational access to climate finance, city pipelines, and innovative instruments. Coordinate CHAMP's advocacy on subnational access to finance with partners, developing a set of concrete "asks" for MDBs and climate funds and supporting political engagement at international climate and finance events. Support CEF colleagues in at least two CHAMP-endorsing countries to ensure country platforms and allow for subnational participation in governance and pipeline decisions. Support Senior Urban and Regional Economist coordinate technical assistance in Kenya and Colombia, ensuring climate strategies and investment plans incorporate subnational priorities and identify domestic and international finance opportunities Support Head of National Action coordinate response to RSLs from four CHAMP-endorsing countries where these relate to climate finance. Capture, synthesise and communicate lessons learned from all programme activities. Maintain detailed and up-to-date project plans for all deliverables using Asana, with clear milestones, risk registers, and mitigation measures, ensuring proactive communication with the Director and Project Board. Oversee budgeting, contracting, and financial monitoring for the Climate Finance workstream. Team Leadership and Diplomatic Engagement (40%) Develop and maintain strategic relationships with Ministries of Finance, MDBs, national development banks, climate funds, and other finance institutions to influence subnational finance reform agendas. Position WRI and CHAMP as experts on subnational climate finance, representing the programme in external events and cross-institutional platforms, and author regular articles on subnational access to climate finance Coordinate across WRI workstreams, country offices, and development team on CHAMP-related activities, and ensure integration of CHAMP activities, lessons learned and insights into WRI's broader research, policy, and advocacy priorities. Collaborate closely with: a) Head of Governance and Diplomacy on connecting climate finance systems insight to global advocacy and Steering Group priorities, b) Head of National Action on coordinating capacity building and technical support for project preparation in Kenya and Colombia. c) Fundraising Manager on developing proposals, cultivating funder relationships, and identifying new investment partnerships for finance-related initiatives. d) C40 and GCoM to coordinate programmatic delivery, technical support and advocacy for improving subnational access to finance Support Director of Urban Efficiency and Climate, Project Board and WRI Ambassadors with all necessary information for decision-making, progress monitoring, and stakeho

title: Operations Support Consultant, Ethiopia
description: This role was posted on August 4, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we work to deploy a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. Do you have experience managing operations, coordinating logistics, and supporting programs in fast-paced environments? Are you passionate about building the operational systems that enable teams to deliver lifesaving impact? If so, you may be the next Operations Support Consultant with our Ethiopia Program. Reporting to the Finance and Operations Director, Ethiopia, the Operations Support Consultant plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day operations of Last Mile Health's Ethiopia program. The consultant will help ensure staff can travel safely, offices are well equipped, vendors are managed effectively, and operational systems run smoothly to enable high-quality program delivery. Working at the intersection of operations, finance, and program teams, the consultant will coordinate logistics, procurement, events, and administrative activities while promoting efficiency, transparency, and value for money. The role will help ensure resources are managed responsibly and that operational support enables teams to focus on delivering impact for the communities we serve. This role is based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia and is open to candidates who are located in and have work authorization in Ethiopia. Consultancy Details Project Duration: September, 2026 - June, 2027 Commitment: Up to 35 hours per week Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Fees: Monthly fees of $1300 USD Scope of Work Logistics & Travel Management End-to-end management of international and domestic travel for staff and consultants, including flights, accommodation, and ground transportation. Facilitate visa applications and provide necessary documentation for staff traveling across various international borders. Lead the logistical planning for training events, conferences, workshops, and retreats (venue sourcing, catering, equipment rentals, and participant travel). Processing import/export documents such as invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading. Ensuring all logistics and operations-related activities comply with organizational, local and donor laws and conditions. Procurement & Vendor Management Identify, evaluate, and select vendors for office supplies, IT equipment, and professional services in alignment with Last Mile Health procurement policies. Maintain a database of preferred vendors and regularly review service level agreements (SLAs) to ensure quality and cost-effectiveness. Negotiate rates with hotels, airlines, and other service providers to efficiently utilize allocated budget by balancing lowest-price criteria with quality and reliability to maximize impact (Value for money). Assessing supplier performance on quality, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness after delivery. Maintaining detailed records of all transactions, including purchase requisitions, quotations, and vendor contracts to allow for audit trails. Maintain an up-to-date inventory of office supplies and fixed assets (laptops, furniture, etc.). Monitor stock levels and initiate timely procurement to ensure zero downtime for staff. Financial Integration & Compliance Initiate formal payment requests and ensure all vendor invoices are matched with Purchase Orders (POs) and delivery notes. Work closely with the Finance Team to ensure timely settlement of bills and reconciliation of monthly purchase orders/travel advances. Maintain meticulous digital and physical records of all procurement and travel transactions for internal and external audits. Required Qualifications Demonstrated experience working in INGO in Ethiopia on Operations such as procurement, logistics, Asset registry and Store management, HR Support. Ability to work cooperatively and collaboratively with all levels of employees, management, and external stakeholders to maximize performance, creativity, problem solving, and results Ability to work independently and clearly communicate needs and expectations from team members and management. Attention to detail, deadlines, and quality of delivery Demonstrated experience working in operations for non-governmental organizations. About Last Mile Health Last Mile Health (LMH) saves lives in the world's most remote communities by partnering with governments to bring critical primary care services to the doorsteps of people living in the last mile. LMH is a registered 501(c)3 non-profit organization and currently works in Ethiopia, Ghana, Liberia, Malawi, Uganda, and Sierra Leone with US offices in Boston. For more information, visit www.lastmilehealth.org. We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity at LMH. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

title: Terms of Reference Yegna Gize Program: Data Collectors
description: Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 since then has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and her livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. 1. Background Girl Effect aims to address the challenges faced by young people in accessing sustainable livelihoods and entrepreneurial opportunities across Ethiopia. In many regions, youth face high unemployment rates, limited access to resources, and a lack of knowledge about viable business opportunities. Girl Effect seeks to empower young people by building their skills, fostering entrepreneurship, and supporting the establishment of profitable businesses. The Yegna Gize program is a three-year initiative (Dec 2024–Dec 2027) funded to empower Ethiopian youth by fostering positive mindsets, transforming community attitudes, and advancing gender inclusivity in leadership and economic participation. 2. Objective Girl Effect is updating its roster of freelance data collectors and would like to request CVs from interested data collectors. The main objective of the data collection or assessment is to quantify and assess mindset shifts and knowledge gain through the program interventions, and to capture regional-level challenges and learnings for program management and adaptations. 3. Scope of Work The Data Collectors will be responsible for gathering high-quality data from youth beneficiaries residing in: Amhara Region: ALBUKO, DESSIE, DESSIE ZURIYA, HAYKE, KALU, KOMBOLCHA, KUTABER, TEHULEDERE Central Ethiopia Region: HOSSANA, LEMO, SHAGSHOGO, SORO, ATOTA ULA, WERA, WERADEJO, ANGACHA, DAMBOYA, TEMBARO Oromia Region: ASELLA, BEKOJI, AD'A (BISHOFTU), ADAMA, ADAMI TULU, ARSI NEGELLE, BATU, DODOLA, SHASHEME, WONDO Sidama Region: ALETA CHUKO, ALETA WENDO, DALE, DARA, DERARA, HAWASSA, HAWASSA ZURIYA, SHEBE DINO, TULA, WONDOGENET South Ethiopia Region: ABELA ABAYA, BODITI, BOLOSO SORE, DAMOT PULASA, DAMOT WOIDE, GESUBA, HUMBO, OFA, SODO, SODO ZURIYA Tigray Region: SHIRE, ENDERTA, MEKELLE, MEKELLE ZURIYA, MAICHEW, MOHONI, ABIADI, ADAWA, AXUM, TAHTAY MAYCHEW Key responsibilities include: Administering digital or paper-based pre-training and post-training surveys. Conducting Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) or Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) if required. Ensuring accurate data entry and real-time synchronization with the central database. Verifying participant demographic consistency and capturing their responses accordingly. Duration: August 2026 – December 2027 based on call Locations: Amhara, Tigray, Oromia, Sidama, South Ethiopia and Central Ethiopia Engagement: Data collectors will be contacted and engaged based on the need for data collection at the time. Engagements will be assigned on an as-needed basis, depending on the scope, location, and timing of each specific assessment 3.1 Methods To ensure high-quality data and impactful of the Yegna Gize Program, the following Mixed-Methods Approach is used: Quantitative Administered via mobile devices (KoboToolbox/ODK) to all sampled participants to measure knowledge gain in growth mindset,entrepreneurship and other behavioural changes. Real-time cross-referencing of participant information against the provided participant list to ensure 80% young women and 5% vulnerable group representation. Qualitative Conducting longitudinal study to gather the impact of the programs and its learning Conducting FGD and KII for deep dive understanding of the program impacts and qualities Sample size The sample size will be determined based on program activities and available data during the interventions with a confidence level for a 95% margin of errors. Quality Assurance The data collector must adhere to guidance provided by MEL and program leads for gathering information with pre and post activity interventions. This will help to capture changes due to the program interventions across the journey the participants passed through. Requirements and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Statistics,Information management

title: Chief of Section, Institutional Capacity-Building and Policy Support
description: Job Description This position provides the unique opportunity of joining the team of a new international organisation, contributing to its lasting construction and influencing its future trajectory. ‍ Our Mission The OSC : The Organisation of Southern Cooperation (OSC) is an international intergovernmental organisation, founded in January 2020 by countries from across the Global South, to “contribute to the equitable, just, and prosperous social transformation of societies by promoting balanced and inclusive education, in order to attain the fundamental rights to liberty, justice, dignity, sustainability, social cohesion, and material and immaterial security for the peoples of the world”. The main functions of the Department of SEED are, accordingly, to: Provide Technical support, from a systematic perspective, in order to build balanced and inclusive educational systems Provide technical support and institutional capacity building in the areas of systemic governance, curricula, teacher training and assessments Host and administer the OSC Institute for Training General Description Under the overall authority of the Secretary General and the direct supervision of the Under- Secretary-General for Systemic and Endogenous Educational Development (SEED), the Chief of Section, Institutional Capacity Building and Policy Support will be responsible for providing the technical guidance and support to Member States in governance and policy articulation adopting a systemic approach framework. Essential Job Functions Support Member states in review and analysis of their existing sectoral policies within the framework of a complex systemic approach; Collaborate with Member States to articulate their policy frameworks, mechanisms, and processes following a systemic approach to governance and policy articulation; Offer technical support to Member States in enhancing their institutional capabilities to work adopting a systemic approach of governance; Develop and maintain strong partnerships and stakeholder engagement with Ministry officials, policy institutes, higher education and TVET apparatus in the Member States to realize the Balanced and Inclusive Education agenda; Lead the development of modules for articulation of the Universal Declaration of Balanced and Inclusive Education and the Global Guide of Ethics, Principles, Policies, and Practices in Balanced and Inclusive Education for the enhancement of understanding of OSC staff; Implement the strategic plan and subsequent annual work plans for the section; Work closely with the section on curricular reforms, training, and assessment to ensure integrated and effective support to Member States in all aspects related to systems enhancement and endogenous development; Project-manage, monitor, evaluate, and report on the Section’s projects and initiatives; Prepare, present, and communicate high-quality executive reports for the USG SEED; Assist with the maintenance of SEED’s institutional presence, including the maintenance of relationships within governmental, academic, and non-governmental organisations. Education, Experience And Qualifications Master’s degree (or higher) in Educational Administration, public policy or other related fields. At least 5-7 years of direct work experience in the area of public policy and institutional strengthening with systemic thinking approach; At least 5 years of work experience around higher education transformation / TVET. Strong proven experience of liaising with stakeholders such as government ministries and institutions, policy institutes, think tanks, etc.; Demonstrated understanding of and experience in executing complex systemic thinking approaches; Strong oral and written communication skills; Ability to draw clear, concise, and executable work plans; Strong conceptual and systemic thinking skills and ability to develop long-term strategies; Ability to operate sensitively and effectively in a multicultural environment and deal with cross-cultural sensitivity; Ability to work in a fast-paced new establishment shouldering multiple responsibilities simultaneously. Proficiency (reading, writing and speaking) in English as well as in one other OSC’s official languages (Spanish, French and Arabic) is mandatory.
